news.headline: Crude Oil WTI Falls -2.09% to $94.07/bbl; Brent -1.77%
news.what_happened: WTI crude oil declined sharply by 2.09% to $94.07 per barrel over the weekend/overnight session, with Brent also down 1.77% to $97.53. Natural gas also fell 1.31%. The broad energy complex selloff suggests demand-side concerns or supply-surplus developments.
news.why_it_matters: Crude is the dominant input cost driver for airlines (35-40% OPEX), tyre manufacturers (60-70% input via synthetic rubber and carbon black), paint companies (40-50% of raw materials as crude derivatives), and auto OEMs. A $2/bbl fall in crude translates to hundreds of crores in annualized savings for these sectors.

news.headline: US 10-Year Treasury Yield Surges +1.03% to 4.998%, Near Critical 5% Level
news.what_happened: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose sharply by 1.03% to 4.998%, brushing up against the psychologically key 5% threshold. This reflects persistent concerns about US fiscal deficit and sticky inflation expectations.
news.why_it_matters: A US 10Y yield at or above 5% historically triggers FII outflows from emerging markets including India. Rate-sensitive Indian sectors (banks, NBFCs, real estate) face valuation compression risk. However, the fact that S&P 500 still closed +0.17% suggests equity markets are currently absorbing the rate pressure.

news.headline: Asian Markets Rally: Nikkei +1.38% to 65,019; Hang Seng +0.56%
news.what_happened: Japan's Nikkei 225 surged 1.38% to 65,019, outperforming all major global indices. Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 0.56% to 24,888. The broad Asian rally reflects positive risk sentiment to start the week.
news.why_it_matters: A strong Asia session is a constructive pre-market signal for India. FIIs are more likely to be net buyers on a day with positive regional cues. Broad market (Nifty 50 stocks) benefits from this global risk-on backdrop.

news.headline: S&P 500 +0.17%, Nasdaq +0.40% — US Markets Post Modest Gains
news.what_happened: US equity markets closed mildly higher: S&P 500 gained 0.17% to 7,650.50 and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.40% to 26,522.55. Gains were moderate amid the rising yield backdrop.
news.why_it_matters: Positive US market close provides a constructive backdrop. Nasdaq outperformance is a mild positive for Indian IT. The modest magnitude suggests caution — equity bulls are fighting the bond yield headwind.

news.headline: Gold Dips -0.53% to $4,401/oz — Risk-On Signal
news.what_happened: Gold fell 0.53% to $4,401.60/oz. Silver also slipped -0.54%.
news.why_it_matters: A fall in gold indicates risk-on globally — investors are moving from safe havens to equities. This is positive for cyclical sectors. Mildly negative for gold loan NBFCs (MUTHOOTFIN, MANAPPURAM) short-term.
